races.name: Weatherbys nhstallions.co.uk Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Viscountess Nelson
runners_data.note: Class advantage with OR 107 and recent win, suits front-running style with Henderson's 48-day preparation gap.
runners_data.comment: Plumpton runner-up; something to find with the Elliott runners but open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Won Irish maiden point in April last year; stepped up from her hurdles debut to open her account in this sphere at Perth (2m4f, good) in April; carries a 7lb penalty but is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Elated
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up in trip with solid RPR 112, Pauling's poor 14-day record (1/18) creates question marks.
runners_data.spotlight: Promising efforts when finishing third in her two runs over hurdles, over 2m at Chepstow and Warwick; looks sure to be suited by this step up in trip and shouldn't be far away.

runners_data.name: My Lady d'Ex
runners_data.note: Hold-up style facing hurdles debut after poor bumper form, 27-day gap insufficient preparation time.
runners_data.comment: Attracted some market support but was last of the nine finishers on debut at Newton Abbot
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 19l and 33l in her two bumpers; steps up in trip on her hurdles debut and needs to show significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Evening Tess
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up type with strong recent second, benefits from Skelton's 10/27 record and trip increase.
runners_data.spotlight: Showing steady improvement with each run, latest when runner-up on her handicap debut at Newton Abbot (2m2f, good) four weeks ago; looks sure to be suited by this step up in trip and holds claims.

runners_data.name: Frenati
runners_data.note: Front-runner needs to prove she can jump after Newton Abbot fall, quick 14-day turnaround suggests confidence.
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner and she looks an interesting recruit to hurdling; needs a close look
runners_data.spotlight: Landed bumper at Stratford (2m, soft) in March; fell at the first flight on her hurdles debut at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good; 4-1) two weeks ago; steps up in trip and should run well provided that fall hasn't left a mark.

runners_data.name: Maria Mes
runners_data.note: Lightly raced unknown quantity returning after 161-day absence, hurdles debut against proven opposition.
runners_data.comment: Outpaced and comfortably held at Sandown but did go off only 11-2
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in her two runs in bumpers; steps up in trip on her hurdles debut but probably best watched until she shows more.

races.paceDynamic: Viscountess Nelson and Frenati will set the early gallop as the confirmed front runners, with Viscountess Nelson likely to take the lead given her stronger recent form after Frenati's fall last time. With only six runners and two keen leaders, this should produce a genuine gallop that will test stamina over the 2m3f trip. Elated will track the pace in third, while Evening Tess and the two hurdles debutants will need to make ground from behind. This honest pace strongly favours horses that can travel prominently and have the class to sustain their effort, benefiting front-running and prominent types over hold-up horses who may find too much to do.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Viscountess Nelson leads and dictates fractions without serious pressure from Frenati
scenarios.body: Her class advantage (OR 107, won last time) allows her to control the race and kick clear approaching the final flight. The honest gallop suits her proven stamina and Bowen can time her effort perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Frenati repeats her falling tendency or refuses to race aggressively after her Newton Abbot fall
scenarios.body: Viscountess Nelson gets an easy lead but lacks the pressure to produce her best, allowing Elated or Evening Tess to close late with their superior RPRs. The tactical pace becomes a sprint finish that favours horses with turn of foot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dual Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If both Viscountess Nelson and Frenati engage in a sustained speed duel through the early and middle stages
scenarios.body: Their mutual pace pressure creates opportunities for the closers, with Evening Tess perfectly positioned to benefit from her progressive profile and strong recent second. Harry Skelton can time his challenge as the leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Frenati Redemption Story
scenarios.trigger: If Frenati jumps cleanly and shows the form that won her Stratford bumper to challenge Viscountess Nelson throughout
scenarios.body: Her front-running style creates the strongest gallop, but her class from that bumper win allows her to sustain the effort better than the favourite. Twiston-Davies rides a confident race to make amends for the recent fall.

watchPoints.text: Frenati's jumping at the first flight after falling there two weeks ago at Newton Abbot
How aggressively Viscountess Nelson breaks from the stalls given her front-running style needs early position
Whether Evening Tess can travel kindly in behind given the likely honest gallop will test her finishing kick
Elated's ability to handle the step up to 2m3f as she's only raced over 2m in both hurdles starts
Maria Mes showing any market moves given her 161-day absence and hurdles debut against stronger opposition

races.name: Sun Racing The Home Of Racing Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Gore Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to likely pace scenario, but 195 days off the track raises significant fitness concerns despite his class advantage.
runners_data.comment: Two hurdle wins this summer; promising chase debut; faded latest but still has potential
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner and won two hurdles races at Newton Abbot last summer; best of three runs over fences when runner-up at Taunton (2m2f, good to firm) in November when last seen; should go close if he is ready to roll.

runners_data.name: Doctor Glide
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with amateur jockey aboard, recent point wins suggest improved form but poor chase record remains a worry.
runners_data.comment: Ex-Irish maiden who been pulled up and tailed off in his two handicaps for this yard
runners_data.spotlight: Showed little in four runs over fences when trained in Ireland, or in three runs over hurdles for current yard; won a couple of points over 2m4f last month but this is a different ball game on his handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Atreides
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose visor transformation in December needs confirming after disappointing comeback run 19 days ago.
runners_data.comment: Dual slow-ground chase winner at around 2m4f; good effort latest; each-way player.
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent sort who was successful in first two attempts in visor, in December, including over C&D (heavy); should have benefitted from his first run for four months when sixth of nine at Worcester (2m4f, good) last month; visor returns to replace cheekpieces and won't be far away.

runners_data.name: A Little Something
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts her in the firing line early, but her breakthrough Stratford win suggests she's finally learning the chase game.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up off today's mark on last two appearances; likely contender again
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark on her 13th start under rules, and her fourth attempt over fences, when accounting for two rivals (only one other completed) at Stratford (2m3f, good to firm) last month; runs off the same mark and this is tougher but still holds claims.

runners_data.name: Wellwillya
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace setup perfectly, and his February course win proves Fontwell effectiveness despite poor recent form.
runners_data.spotlight: Second of two wins over fences came at this track (2m5f, heavy) in February 2025; comfortably held when fourth of seven finishers over C&D (good) last month and needs to show improvement.

runners_data.name: Footloose Man
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with outstanding Fontwell record including course and distance win 17 days ago, but non-runner status creates uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Dual course winner last season; a possible if recent reappearance run brought him on
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins have been at this track, the latest over C&D (good) 17 days ago; must come into the equation on track that clearly suits.

races.paceDynamic: Doctor Glide will take this field along as the sole confirmed front runner, with Atreides, A Little Something and Footloose Man likely to press him early from prominent positions. With four horses wanting to race handily, the pace could become contested in the opening mile, particularly if the prominent runners don't settle behind Doctor Glide. This tactical squeeze should set up a true test of stamina over the final half-mile, creating a race shape that strongly favours the hold-up horses who can avoid the early pace battle and deliver late challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners press Doctor Glide early and create genuine pace pressure
scenarios.body: The early pace battle will compromise the front division, allowing the patient riders to pick up the pieces in the home straight. Gore Point and Wellwillya benefit most from this tactical scenario with their hold-up styles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Footloose Man's Track Mastery
scenarios.trigger: If Footloose Man can secure an ideal stalking position behind the early leaders
scenarios.body: His four previous wins at Fontwell give him a crucial edge, and he can time his challenge perfectly from a prominent but not pressured position. The consistent good ground matches his preferences exactly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Suits
scenarios.trigger: If Doctor Glide is allowed an easy lead with the prominent horses settling behind him
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the front division to maintain their advantage, with the race becoming a test of class rather than stamina. Doctor Glide's recent point wins suggest improved form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Atreides Bounces Back
scenarios.trigger: If the visor continues to transform Atreides and his 19-day break has sharpened him up
scenarios.body: His December course and distance win in heavy ground proves his effectiveness here, and the good ground won't inconvenience him. The prominent style works if he can avoid the early pace squeeze.

watchPoints.text: Doctor Glide's amateur jockey could misjudge the pace given the early pressure from prominent runners
Gore Point's 195-day absence may show early despite his superior class credentials
Atreides needs the visor to have the same transformative effect as his December wins
Footloose Man's non-runner status despite being well-suited to the conditions and course
Wellwillya's hold-up style requires the early pace to develop as expected to be competitive

races.name: Celebrating The Life Of Trevor Schooley Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Sun Joy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who may struggle with the trip drop from 2m5f winning distance, coming off a poor 17-length defeat at this track last month
runners_data.comment: Back in prime form when last seen in the autumn; contender if ready to roll after break
runners_data.spotlight: Dual winning hurdler over about 2m5f; beaten 17l at this track (2m3f) last month following a six-month break and not sure that the drop back in trip will be in his favour.

runners_data.name: Granny Hawkins
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer on a three-timer roll with progressive profile, perfectly suited to a tactical race setup under patient Tom Bellamy
runners_data.comment: Up in grade after her two Hereford wins but might still be improving
runners_data.spotlight: Has got her act together over hurdles and completed a three-timer at Stratford (2m, good) in April; looks the sort to continue to progress and looks the one they all have to beat despite a 6lb rise.

runners_data.name: Almuhit
runners_data.note: Prominent style with mixed recent form, returning to hurdles after flat racing stint but has won over obstacles before for previous trainer
runners_data.comment: Two front-running wins over 2m in four-runner Flat races last year; back up from 1m6f
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins over hurdles in February/March 2025 when trained by Gary Brown; has raced mainly on the Flat for current yard, winning twice at Newbury last summer; fourth in valuable 24-runner handicap hurdle at Punchestown (2m3f, yielding) in April; should go close if running to form.

runners_data.name: Break Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with limited form credentials, making hurdles return for new trainer Luke Dace after disappointing Uttoxeter effort
runners_data.comment: Two modest runs in low-grade AW races since leaving Olly Murphy
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came in a Perth maiden hurdle in August last year when trained by Olly Murphy; last of ten finishers at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) on first hurdles start for current trainer 17 days ago; needs to return to form to figure.

runners_data.name: Sixty Plus
runners_data.note: Front-running leader with 88-day break, class advantage off lower mark than his Worcester four-timer completion but faces stronger opposition
runners_data.comment: Well beaten following an 11-week absence at Wetherby last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a four-timer when scoring at Worcester (2m4f, good) last September off 1lb lower; well held in better company since, he should appreciate the drop in grade but this trip is plenty short enough.

races.paceDynamic: Sixty Plus is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start, setting a sustainable pace without early pressure. Sun Joy and Almuhit will track prominently behind the leader, while Granny Hawkins and Break Point are likely to be held up at the rear in a slowly-run affair. With minimal early pace pressure, the race will develop into a tactical contest where horses need to be produced with well-timed challenges. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can deliver late kicks, as the lack of early pace will leave plenty in the tank for the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady throughout and no prominent tracker applies early pressure
scenarios.body: The lack of pace allows hold-up horses to conserve energy and unleash devastating finishing kicks. Granny Hawkins and Break Point benefit most from this tactical setup with their patient styles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Sun Joy or Almuhit apply pressure to Sixty Plus turning for home
scenarios.body: The race develops into a battle between the front three, with the prominent horses having positional advantage. Their forward positions prove decisive when the hold-up horses leave too much to do.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wire-To-Wire Upset
scenarios.trigger: If Sixty Plus maintains his gallop and the field fails to close the gap
scenarios.body: The leader's class advantage tells as he controls every call without serious pressure until too late. His four-timer completing form at Worcester suggests he can repeat when conditions suit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling and the race turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery where positioning at the last hurdle matters more than running style. Any horse close enough at the business end can capitalize on the chaotic finish.

watchPoints.text: Sixty Plus could steal this if he gets an easy lead and the field allows him too much rope turning for home
Sun Joy's fitness after that poor Fontwell effort last month, where he was beaten 17 lengths following a six-month break
Granny Hawkins' jumping under pressure if she has to be produced earlier than ideal due to pace dynamics
Break Point's hurdles readiness on stable debut for Luke Dace after flat racing focus recently
Almuhit's hurdles sharpness returning to obstacles after summer flat racing campaign for current trainer

races.name: Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Special John
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in career-best form with 25-day freshening break, needs to handle class rise but tactical advantage likely
runners_data.comment: Beaten favourite on last three runs, but back on track last time out; remains of interest.
runners_data.spotlight: 3-5 over fences, his latest success at Bangor (3m, good) last month a career-best; needs to step up again in this better contest but going the right way.

runners_data.name: Ballyfinn
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits race shape but quick 8-day turnaround after disappointing follow-up to C&D win raises questions
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark on his fifth attempt over fences, over C&D (good) last month; nowhere near that level here (2m3f, good) eight days later but maybe he can return to form back to his winning distance.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Hold-up style disadvantaged by likely modest pace, concerning pull-up last time and Nick Scholfield training record
runners_data.comment: Landed back-to-back wins at Hereford over 3m1f on good this spring.
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice at Hereford over 3m1f in the spring but has found life tougher since; pulled up at Warwick (3m1f, good) three weeks ago; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Gata Ban
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer facing tactical disadvantage despite 4-day quick turnaround from Worcester victory
runners_data.comment: 0-7 over fences but a close second at Fontwell latest, caught late on; leading player.
runners_data.spotlight: No match for Ballyfinn when having to settle for second place over C&D (good) last month, but opened her account over fences at Worcester (2m7f, good) on Saturday; shoulders a 7lb penalty and this looks tougher.

races.paceDynamic: Special John and Ballyfinn both possess prominent racing styles and will likely dispute the early lead in this small field. With no confirmed front-runners beyond Special John, the pace should be sustainable rather than cut-throat, allowing the leaders to dictate terms throughout the 3m2f journey. The lack of genuine pace pressure means horses that can position handily and stay strong will have a significant advantage over hold-up performers like Edgewell and Gata Ban, who may struggle to make up ground in a slowly-run race. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position close to the pace and have the stamina to sustain their effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Special John Sustains Momentum
scenarios.trigger: If Special John can replicate his career-best Bangor form and handle the step up in class
scenarios.body: His prominent style suits the likely pace scenario and Matt Griffiths can dictate terms from the front without serious pressure. The 25-day break since his impressive win keeps him fresh for this step up in grade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Ballyfinn Returns to Winning Form
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyfinn bounces back from his disappointing effort eight days after his course and distance victory
scenarios.body: Anthony Honeyball's charge proved he handles these conditions when winning over C&D and his prominent style allows him to track Special John before challenging. The extra weight from his recent win may not stop him if returning to that level.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Gata Ban Benefits from Fitness
scenarios.trigger: If the 4-day turnaround since her Worcester victory brings peak fitness rather than fatigue
scenarios.body: Her recent course form is solid and the quick return could have her spot-on, though her hold-up style faces the tactical disadvantage of a likely modest pace. Neil Mulholland's 2/14 record suggests he times his runners well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Edgewell Redeems Recent Form
scenarios.trigger: If Edgewell can rediscover his Hereford spring form and overcome his Warwick pull-up
scenarios.body: His hold-up style needs a strong pace to be effective, which seems unlikely here given the small field composition. The 21-day break may have refreshed him but his recent form trend is concerning.

watchPoints.text: Special John's jumping under pressure if challenged - any mistakes could prove costly in this small field
Ballyfinn's attitude after his flat effort following his course win - needs to show the same enthusiasm
Edgewell's willingness to race after pulling up at Warwick - early signs of travel will reveal his wellbeing
Gata Ban's position turning for home given her hold-up style may need the leaders to weaken significantly
The pace through the middle stages - if too slow it will heavily favor the prominent pair over the hold-up horses

races.name: Jewson Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: A Tickatickatiming
runners_data.comment: Bumper/maiden hurdle winner here in 2023; in good form and should be close up again
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success over hurdles came in a Plumpton maiden in November 2023; has shown bits of form since but was pulled up at Plumpton (2m, good) when last seen; difficult to enthuse over.

runners_data.name: Our Brother John
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making rules debut after long point-to-point campaign, hard to assess
runners_data.spotlight: Achieved little in three runs under rules in 2023; has been running in points since but last win in that sphere was also in 2023; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Galactic Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in career-best form with three straight placings, benefits from patient pace
runners_data.comment: Best of three runs for new stable when third at Taunton last month; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Useful on the Flat in his prime; yet to win over hurdles, but has made the frame on his last three starts, since returning from a lengthy absence; down to a career-low mark and holds claims.

runners_data.name: Kates Choice
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who broke her maiden three weeks ago, 4lb rise looks workable
runners_data.comment: 25l off the winner when second two runs back; fell early here two weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark under rules at the 13th attempt at Ffos Las (2m4f, good to soft) three weeks ago; 4lb rise isn't harsh and she should be competitive.

runners_data.name: Easter Icon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course win, 5lb claimer adds tactical complexity but lacks experience
runners_data.comment: Course winner who showed signs of a revival at Stratford last month; could be dangerous
runners_data.spotlight: Has six wins on the Flat; sole success in this sphere came at this track (2m5f, good) in August 2024; still 6lb above his winning mark but was still in contention when brought down at the last flight over C&D (good) in April; holds place claims.

runners_data.name: Kylenoe Dancer
runners_data.note: Prominent horse with course and distance win, improved effort last time suggests return to form
runners_data.comment: Has some long absences in her profile and was pulled when returning from one in March
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came over C&D in May last year; seemed to need first run back from ten-month absence and fared better when third of seven at Worcester (2m4f, good) 19 days ago; should be spot on now and holds claims.

runners_data.name: Mistress Fox
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare running best over hurdles, runner-up here last month gives course advantage
runners_data.comment: Better run last time out and she's bred for this longer distance
runners_data.spotlight: Is gradually getting the hang of things over hurdles, running up to her best when runner-up here (2m5f, good) last month; should not be far away.

runners_data.name: Charles Morin
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping up in trip after staying-on fourth, longer distance should suit
runners_data.comment: Closely matched with Balgowan on revised terms and looks set to go well again; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't raced much over hurdles and shaped as though this step up in trip will suit when staying on into fourth at Plumpton (2m, good to soft) in March; beaten in low-grade contests on Flat since; place claims.

runners_data.name: Dunaden Island
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with poor hurdles record, 5lb claimer may struggle tactically
runners_data.comment: Ex-pointer; fourth at big odds on rules debut but well beaten twice since; handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: 1-9 in points; has shown little in four starts over hurdles; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Maestrow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse prone to fading, handicap debut for strong yard but poor recent form
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown little so far; steps up in trip on handicap debut; major yard; worth a market check.

races.paceDynamic: Dunaden Island will take this race by the scruff of the neck from the start, with Tickatickatiming, Easter Icon and Kylenoe Dancer settling just behind in a prominent group. The pace will be steady rather than searching, as Dunaden Island has no genuine pace pressure and can dictate terms through the early stages. This will create a patient, building gallop that suits the hold-up horses perfectly, as the large contingent of backmarkers including Galactic Jack, Kates Choice, Mistress Fox and Charles Morin will get the patient ride they need before launching late challenges. The sustainable pace and weak early speed strongly favours hold-up horses who can time their runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Dunaden Island sets an uncontested lead and the pace stays modest through halfway
scenarios.body: The patient gallop allows the backmarkers to conserve energy and unleash telling late runs, with the hold-up brigade sweeping past the tiring leaders. Galactic Jack, Kates Choice, Mistress Fox and Charles Morin all benefit from the tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens approaching the final mile and the hold-up horses get caught flat-footed
scenarios.body: Easter Icon or Kylenoe Dancer can quicken from their forward positions while the backmarkers struggle for room or momentum. The prominent horses strike the ideal balance between position and finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner steals it
scenarios.trigger: If Dunaden Island gets such an easy time that he retains enough stamina to resist late challenges
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage through fractions that are too slow for the field to reel him back in time. His front-running style pays dividends when the tactics fall perfectly into place.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so pedestrian that it becomes a sprint finish where class tells
scenarios.body: The race turns into a pure speed test over the final two furlongs, favouring horses with the highest ratings regardless of running style. Form horses with proven class edge out the outsiders in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Dunaden Island could get such an easy lead with inexperienced claimer Corcoran that he steals a march
Easter Icon's 5lb claimer Ryder may struggle with pace judgement if the race develops into tactical battle
Kylenoe Dancer needed his comeback run and could improve significantly for that racecourse gallop
Our Brother John brings unknown point-to-point form but has been absent from rules racing since 2023
Charles Morin showed improved stamina last time and this trip extension could unlock more improvement

races.name: Cathedral Wealth Ahead Of The Field Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jack The Savage
runners_data.note: Front runner with new jockey Sean Bowen taking over, 78 days off but proven over similar trips on good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Landed a weak handicap at Hereford (3m1f, good) in March; never threatened off 2lb higher at Southwell (3m, good) last time; Sean Bowen rides for the first time so may well have a say.

runners_data.name: Alan Bresil
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who achieved little over hurdles, trainer struggling at 0/8 in last 14 days but recent proximity suggests some form
runners_data.spotlight: Has achieved little over hurdles; second of two finishers at Huntingdon (3m1f, good to firm) 16 days ago.

runners_data.name: Fravanco
runners_data.note: Prominent racer suited by this distance based on course and distance runner-up effort, 47 days since last run could be ideal
runners_data.comment: Beaten 61l on handicap debut last month; up markedly in trip for this second go
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 over hurdles but seemed suited by the new trip when runner-up over C&D (good) in April; should not be far away.

runners_data.name: Muskerry Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won last time in hunter chase over similar trip, has concerning tendency to fade in finish which is problematic
runners_data.comment: Joined Dan Skelton for £17,000 after winning Wexford hunter chase last month; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Dual point winner who came good under rules with front-running success in Wexford hunter chase (2m7f, good to yielding; refitted cheekpieces) last month; changed hands subsequently for £17,000 and has to be over interest back over hurdles for top new yard.

runners_data.name: Good Girl Rachel
runners_data.note: Prominent style runner carrying bottom weight at 147lbs, limited hurdles form but cheekpieces applied for recent run
runners_data.comment: This longer trip is probably a good move for her handicap debut; tries cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown only modest form over hurdles, including on handicap debut when fourth of eight at Ffos Las (3m, good to soft) three weeks ago in first-time cheekpieces which are replaced by visor here; hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Jack The Savage will lead from the front with Fravanco and Good Girl Rachel tracking in prominent positions through the early stages. The modest field size and single confirmed front runner suggests a steady, uncontested gallop over this staying trip on good ground. Alan Bresil and Muskerry Rock will be held up at the back, looking to time their challenges late. This pace setup strongly favours prominent racers who can stay close to Jack The Savage without having to make up significant ground in the finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Jack The Savage gets an easy lead and dictates terms throughout
scenarios.body: Sean Bowen can control the tempo from the front, saving enough for a sustained kick when the closers challenge. The lack of pace pressure allows the leader to retain stamina reserves for the demanding finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady but one of the prominent runners has more left in the tank
scenarios.body: Fravanco or Good Girl Rachel can stalk Jack The Savage comfortably before unleashing a telling burst in the straight. Their positioning advantage proves decisive over the hold-up horses who face too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Surges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely pedestrian and sets up a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Muskerry Rock uses Harry Skelton's timing to perfection, sweeping past tiring leaders in the final furlong. Alan Bresil could also benefit if the race becomes a pure stamina test with a genuine kick required.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Jack The Savage stops quickly and the prominent trackers also fade
scenarios.body: The moderate early gallop leaves all the front-runners vulnerable to any horse with a finishing kick. Good Girl Rachel's light weight or Alan Bresil's hold-up style could prove advantageous in a slowly-run affair.

watchPoints.text: Muskerry Rock's finishing kick may not materialise given his noted tendency to fade in the final stages despite recent win
Jack The Savage faces first-time partnership with Sean Bowen after 78-day layoff, communication could be crucial in controlling the pace
Fravanco showed clear improvement over this course and distance last time, suggesting the extended trip suits better than shorter hurdle races
Alan Bresil has shown little over hurdles but recent second at Huntingdon suggests some current form, though trainer record is concerning
Good Girl Rachel's 147lbs represents a significant weight advantage in a race where the top weight carries 168lbs
